issued_by.impersonation_disclaimer: Not a human reviewer and not the owner.

part_1_what_was_lost_and_when.cause: an operator disk-cleanup command collected the whole backups directory with a bare *.db glob, kept only the newest-mtime daily and unlinked the rest; the same command then emptied the Trash. Confirmed by the operator from its own session log. Not the production retention code, not the reviewer's named deletions, not the owner.
part_1_what_was_lost_and_when.trash_note: the Trash-emptying step ran minutes after the owner's manual deletion of the hidden evidence directories in the same login window; if any deleted item was still in the Trash then, that step destroyed the last copy. Recorded as aggravation of W-7; nothing is recoverable either way and the sealed-ledger incident a7cea63 stands as adjudicated.

part_2_impact: operationally nil, as adjudicated in conversation: the three archives insured operations completed and validated weeks ago, no governance record pins their digests as a dependency, and disaster recovery rests on the live database plus the current dailies. Their digests above remain the permanent proof they existed.
part_3_not_an_incident: the 2026-08-22, 08-23 and 08-24 daily backups are not missing: the reviewer deleted them by exact name on 2026-08-26 under the owner's disk-cleanup request, keeping the newest two dailies with all manifests retained. No investigation is warranted.

part_4_standing_rule.rule: every cleanup command run by any agent uses an explicit allowlist of exact filenames or anchored patterns; bare wildcards over a directory are forbidden. A cleanup touching data/backups may match only the managed daily pattern alphapilot-full-[0-9]{8}T[0-9]{12}Z.db and never a named archive. No cleanup command ever empties the Trash: the Trash is the owner's undo buffer, not an agent's.
part_4_standing_rule.lineage: extends the no-broad-glob rule from the evidence-cleanup authorization and the W-7 durable-evidence rule to all cleanup surfaces

part_5_forensics_declined: APFS carving on a TRIM-enabled SSD has near-zero odds, would require halting all disk writes mid-review-run, and the impact is nil; the owner's earlier disposition of the archives already treated them as expendable. Declined.
